title: Report on Studying at Lund University
paragraphs: From February 2024, I studied for two months at Lund University in Sweden. Until then I had never been to Europe, and I was anxious about living in an unknown environment. However, I was able to study abroad supported by many people: the lectures by the professors of the Frontier-kai and the International Collaboration Office, study sessions with classmates, and my parents' assistance. I sincerely thank them.

Lund University has its main campus in the city of Lund in Skåne County in southern Sweden, and is the second oldest university in the country. International exchange is lively, and many international students from Japan study there. The city of Lund has a refined Nordic townscape, more than half of the residents are students so it is safe, and since it is a mild region even for Sweden, it was a very easy environment to live in.

For the first month I did my clerkship in Surgery (Surgery Clinic) at Skåne University Hospital in the city of Lund. It is divided into the upper gastrointestinal group, the hepatobiliary-pancreatic group, and the endocrine and soft tissue tumor group, and each group had more than ten doctors. The male-to-female ratio was 5 to 5. I mainly observed surgery in the hepatobiliary-pancreatic group and experienced assisting with suction, ligation and wound closure. I could observe each doctor using the latest technology while demonstrating their specialty, such as a surgeon performing ERCP and endoscopy, a case in which ablation was performed in cooperation with a radiologist during surgery for metastatic liver cancer, and robot-assisted pancreaticoduodenectomy.

For the next month I did my clerkship in Hand Surgery (Hand Surgery Clinic) at Skåne University Hospital in the city of Malmö. In Sweden, hand surgery is a department independent of orthopedics and plastic surgery. The hand surgery at Malmö Hospital is the largest clinic in Sweden, and on some days more than ten operations are performed. The outpatient clinic, ward, operating rooms and rehabilitation room are in the same building, and care was provided with seamless cooperation. I was surprised that medical leeches are used in hand and finger trauma.

Through the clerkships I was able to deeply understand knowledge and procedures in surgery and hand surgery. In addition, I gained valuable learning about Sweden's healthcare system, education, insurance and welfare systems, and culture. In Sweden the Personal number system is widespread, and because patient ID, banks, work, insurance and so on are all linked to it, applications for sick leave and compensation are carried out smoothly. I was also able to learn about differences from Japan in the education system of local medical students and in job hunting. Coming into contact with the knowledge and enthusiasm of the Lund students, I realised my own lack of motivation. The two months of the study abroad were very fulfilling, and besides the clerkships, every day was fresh, with interaction with international students in the dormitory and trips to various countries with friends on holidays. I sincerely thank those who supported me for giving me such a valuable experience as a student. I will make further efforts based on this experience. Thank you.
